full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed, J: This revisional application calls in question the property of the judgment and decree dated 13.11.94 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 5th Court. Dhaka allowing Title Appeal No. 374 of 1990 decreeing the suit after setting aside judgment and decree dated 30.8.90 passed by the Assistant Judge, 3rd Additional Court, Dhaka dismissing Title Suit No. 82 of 1990. 

 6. In view of the provision of section 10(1) of the Presidents Order 16 of 1972. I observe that the Government can cancel or terminate any allotment or can amend the allotment of abandoned property by amending the terms of lease under which the abandoned property is allotted ether permanently or temporary in allotment was made after 25th day of March, 1971 with intimation to the allottee. In this case the cancellation has been made be-fore making any amendment or rectification of the conditions of the deed of agreement of allotment. So the cancellation is illegal. In the case of Zahirul Hoque vs. Ejamul Huq reported in 1981 B.L.D. (AD) 346 the same point was dealt with. The Appellate Division found that the authority can evict the persons with due process of law. The Government or Abandoned Property Authority is no doubt at liberty to evict the person treating him as a monthly tenant by a fresh order but before that it must be shown that the fulfillment of terms of clause of the letter of allotment has been made or the tenant has violated any condition thereof which is lacking in the present case. Since the allotment authority can evict the allotted by making necessary change in the deed of allotment as per provision of section 10(1) of the President's Order 16 of 1972 and Government also can affix standard rent of the suit premises as per law. I have gone through the Judgments of the courts below carefully, meticulously and find that the trial court failed to interpret the provision of section 10(1) of the Presidents Order 16 of 1972 and the terms of the deed of agreement creating the allotment to their true perspective and as a result decision of the trial court dismissing the suit being erroneous has been rightly and legally set aside by the appellate court. I do not find any infirmity or illegality in the judgment of the appellate court in decreeing the suit and there is no failure of justice in the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court. I find no merit in this revision.
